body.statement: For every \(P\in\Delta_{31}\), \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), the signed list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is observable and finite. Its sign vector and signed Sturm--Habicht lifting table are necessary and sufficient for each of the eight oriented systems \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) to have a real solution. After combining the two relative alignments, \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) is a singleton if and only if every accepted cell has zero oscillation in both reconstructed coordinates \(\tau_3\) and \(\tau_4\) and the two alignment images coincide. If this condition fails, the same certificate returns two accepted cells and reconstructed latent witnesses having unequal ATT vectors. These equivalences include vanishing rank coefficients, alignment coincidences, and every compact-box face.
body.justification: This is the requested observable necessary-and-sufficient point-identification classification on the completed merger stratum.
body.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's Proposition 4 identifies parameters under RSM, M, and ID, and their Proposition 5 and Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under the stated TI--LT regular conditions; those results do not classify ATT constancy after one terminal collision. Higgins and Jochmans's Theorem 1 identifies a finite mixture of Markov chains from four consecutive observations under their Assumptions 1--3, including an observable rank condition and type-separating walk conditions, but does not classify this coupled-arm collision fiber or its aggregate-ATT image. Geiger and Meek's Sections 3.3--3.4 show how real quantifier elimination obtains implicit observable constraints and answers identification or bounding questions for polynomial models, without the present causal branch labels or reconstructed counter-witness grammar.
body.consumer: The Dodd--Frank, Norwegian patenting, and ADA analyses can distinguish an observed-law ATT sign from a sign induced by one arbitrary cross-arm merger resolution.
body.proof_tex:
On the maintained one-collision stratum, \(p_d\geq\eta>0\).  Hence \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are observable rational functions of the thirty-two cells of \(P\), with the only denominator \(p_d\).  Multiplication by positive powers of \(p_0p_1\) converts every equality or weak/strict sign in \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\) into an equivalent integer-polynomial sign condition in \((P,\eta,y)\).  The system has finitely many such polynomials because it has ten variables, twelve equalities, three orientation inequalities, finitely many mass inequalities, and two box inequalities for each member of a finite list of reconstructed primitives.

Apply the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition lemma to this finite family in the fixed coordinate order.  The coefficients, leading coefficients, discriminants, resultants, and signed principal subresultant coefficients prescribed in the observable-sign-certificate definition are polynomials only in the remaining coordinates at each projection step.  After all ten coordinates have been eliminated, they are polynomials only in \((P,\eta)\).  Thus \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is finite and observable.  Sign-invariant lifting, including its zero sections, has the following exact equivalence for every \(s\):
\[
 \exists y\;\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{the signed lifting table accepts at least one cell above }(P,\eta).
 \tag{12}
\]
Necessity follows because any solution lies in one lifted cell and realizes its recorded signs.  Sufficiency follows because an accepted sample point satisfies every equality and weak or strict inequality of the original system.  Signed subresultant data determine multiplicities and signs at common roots, so (12) remains valid when a leading coefficient, discriminant, rank coefficient, or inequality boundary vanishes.

By the proved terminal-splitting reduction and quotient invariance,
\[
 \mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 =\bigcup_{s\in\{-1,1\}^3}\ \bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \left\{\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P):
 \mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\right\}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The assumption \(\varnothing\ne\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\) makes (13) nonempty.  A nonempty set in \(\mathbb R^2\) is a singleton exactly when no two of its elements differ.  For two reconstructed points, that difference is nonzero exactly when
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^4
 \left[\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P)
 -\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P)\right]^2>0.
 \tag{14}
\]
All denominators in (14) are positive reconstructed masses; clearing their squares preserves the strict sign.  The observable-sign-certificate definition applies the same projection and lifting to (14) together with both branch systems, for every \((s,\sigma,s',\sigma')\).  It therefore decides the existence of an unequal pair.  Nonexistence is equivalent to zero oscillation within every accepted cell and equality between every pair of nonempty alignment images.  Existence supplies two accepted real-algebraic sample points; reconstruction supplies two compatible latent vectors with unequal ATT.  This proves necessity, sufficiency, and the asserted counter-witness property on zero, alignment-coincidence, and box-contact cells alike.
